description: fib (Fast In Balance) Go networking library, served through its prefork package: a master process starts a child for every two CPUs, each with two Ps and its own heap, and the engine each child runs listens with SO_REUSEPORT, so the children share the ports; every listener is a fib.Binding of that one engine (fib.New), sharing its event loop, task pool and buffer pool. In each child an edge-triggered epoll event loop hands HTTP/1 connections' rounds to a logical worker pool, where each connection is an ordered task that any idle worker may run. Its http package serves HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 (ALPN and prior-knowledge h2c) and, through package http3, HTTP/3 over its own QUIC, all through one handler taking a Context that carries the *http.Request; TLS through package tls on crypto/tls. Default configuration throughout, but for request bodies past 64 KiB, which stream to their handlers as fit, fib's gateway, has them; the certificate on the opt-in TLS hardening listener is picked per handshake through tls.Config.GetCertificate, so a renewed pair is served without a restart. Requests are routed by fib's Router (chi's API with fib's handlers), the same one for every protocol, with path parameters read through Context.Param, and JSON answered through Context.JSON, encoding/json's encoding; the JSON routes sit behind fib's compress middleware (Router.With(compress.New(...))) with fiber's compress settings, the default level (gzip 6) and fasthttp's 200-byte floor, which gzips per request as Accept-Encoding allows. The gRPC profiles' BenchmarkService, protoc-generated with google.golang.org/protobuf messages, is served by fib's grpc package through the same router, so gRPC shares 8080 (h2c) and 8443 (h2 over TLS) with HTTP. nothing blocks fib's workers, as in fit: /delay answers its request, retained through Context.Async, from a timer, /async-db hands its query to a taskpool of as many workers as the database pool has connections, request bodies past 64 KiB stream to their handlers (StreamRequestBody, fit's 64 KiB threshold and buffer), and /echo sends a streamed body back as it arrives through OnBody and WriteNoWait, holding the request body with HoldBody until OnWritable while the client is behind, and /static goes through fib's FileCache, which serves the files from memory and follows the disk through an inotify watch, choosing the pre-compressed twin on disk off Accept-Encoding.
